01.project.v: Willis Temby: Custom Website Design and Build (plus logo redesign)

01.pm.v: Gabe Silva (project coordinator from 21/10/2026, took over from Eleanor Morgan; earlier Tafleen and Mia). Adam Barbarich stays involved at kick-off, design sign-off, pre-launch and post-launch

01.dev_reviewer.v: Raf Baldasso (head of development, across the technical scope since sales)

01.design_hours.v: 34 design hours in the quote, not split between homepage and internals. Revisions and adjustments (dev and design) are a separate 21 hours

01.deliverable.v: Homepage, Contact page, industry landing template, policy/product template, Our People team profile, blog and news/insights template, plus internal page designs as required. Logo: 3 concepts, 2 revision rounds, basic style guide

01.platform.v: WordPress (latest stable), Gravity Forms, Rank Math Premium

01.kickoff_held.v: Yes, 21/07/2026 online. Mia Mammoliti with Isabella and Cameron (Willis Temby). Raf absent

02.drive.v: Willis Temby folder (Drive id 1yaFpFcI1J7SM0lBZ0WMWCfoSVG-Jl8TM): Brand Brief, Home Page Layout, Website 2.0 Flow v2, Product Page mock-up

02.sitemap.v: Whimsical: account-management-team/willis-temby. Approval status not recorded anywhere in the folder

02.existing_site.v: willistemby.com.au on RocketSpark. Audit: about 1 form submission a month against 600+ calls, contact form up to 2 minutes to load, jQuery 1.7.2, placeholder copy live. Client calls it outdated and wants a modern look

02.style_guide.v: No brand style guide exists yet. The logo line item delivers a basic style guide for logo use and colour palettes

02.logo.v: Logo being redesigned by PWD. Figma logo mood board linked in the old MASTER. Sign-off status not recorded

02.moodboard.v: Client moodboard (bold colour pops, kept professional) and AI-generated style ideas in the old MASTER Logo Brief; Brand Brief.docx

02.quote.v: Estimate 5756, Digital Partnership: Custom Website Design and Build for Willis Temby, signed by Isabella Popov 30/06/2026

02.handover.v: Willis Temby Internal Handover Brief, Scott Donovan

03.who.v: Australian-owned, privately operated insurance brokerage, founded 1984, 7 Alvan Street Mount Lawley. Legal entity Willis Temby Insurance Brokers Pty Ltd, AFSL 233 765, ABN 85 009 087 585. Rebranding to "Willis Temby"

03.what.v: Commercial insurance broking and risk advisory: tailored insurance programs, policy program review, claims advocacy, early injury intervention (Praventus)

03.for_whom.v: Mid to large commercial businesses in high-risk sectors (marine, mining and resources, construction, agribusiness, commercial property). Buyers: owners, CFOs, CEOs, MDs, risk managers

03.why_us.v: "Strategic insurance and risk advice designed for complex organisations, backed by deep technical expertise"; forward-thinking advice; proactive claims advocacy and early intervention; 40+ years

03.position.v: Wants to read as credible and established to larger corporates, "corporate but still modern", not hectic like Knightcorp. Must sit clearly apart from Willis Towers Watson (WTW)

03.decision_makers.v: Isabella Breheny (Head of Marketing and Communications, signed as Isabella Popov) runs it day to day. Executive Directors Alex Rowland and Brett Piggott approve at milestones. Cameron (camerong@) sat in the kick-off, role unconfirmed

03.behaviour.v: Fast, considered, decisive. Runs things past the directors and comes back with clear positions. Prefers fortnightly milestone updates over weekly check-ins. Pushes back on scope, not price

04.objective.v: Convert the inbound demand they already get into enquiries from larger corporates. Lead generation and organic search over awareness

04.hero_action.v: Contact us (enquiry form, then call). Pay an Invoice is off the homepage

04.secondary_actions.v: Draft from the menu utilities: Request a quote, Lodge a claim, Lodge workplace injury. Three, so one must drop to a menu link

04.success.v: Match or beat Phoenix Insurance organic traffic (661 a month) within 12 months; long term overtake Centrewest (1,000+ a month); lift form enquiries from about 1 a month

04.broken.v: About 1 form a month against 600+ calls, slow contact form, jQuery 1.7.2 security exposure, placeholder content, no alt tags, multiple H1s, "Powered by RocketSpark" footer, no AI search presence, dated brand

04.keep.v: At least one logo option keeps the current blue (directors). Legal entity name on site. Existing URLs and rankings via SEO migration

05.profile.v: B2B, SME to enterprise, strong mid-market bias. Personal lines exist for existing clients but are not the focus

05.primary_audience.v: Operations directors, CFOs, owners and risk managers in marine, mining and resources, construction, energy, commercial property

05.secondary_audience.v: Aviation, transport, healthcare, manufacturing, professional services, cyber, hospitality. HNW individuals for personal assets

05.worries.v: Assessing whether the broker is credible enough for a complex program and understands their industry, not shopping on price

05.devices.v: Not known. Pull from GA4 once access is granted

05.competitors.v: Centrewest and Knightcorp (named by client), Phoenix Insurance, Bellrock (benchmark). Bellrock Advisory is a liked site, not a competitor

06.value.v: $35,840 ex GST ($39,424 inc GST) fixed estimate at $195 an hour, including the $2,495 logo option. Hosting $45 a month ex GST for 12 months

06.design_allocation.v: 34 design hours inside 155 website hours (Dev 66, PM 26, QA 8, Revisions 21). Logo is its own $2,495 line. Split between homepage and internals not set

06.revisions.v: Design: 2 major rounds per layout. Development: 2 rounds of changes. Logo: 2 rounds on the chosen concept

06.in_scope.v: Logo redesign; WordPress build; mega menu with clickable parents; Gravity Forms (general enquiry, request a quote, lodge a claim, workplace injury, insurance program review); secure PDF storage for claim and injury forms; Pay an Invoice page linking to DEFT (Macquarie); FAQ accordions; blog and insights with filtering; team profiles; EDM integration; LinkedIn feed; testimonials; schema; compliance content and AFSL footer; content migration (placement only, 14 hours); SEO migration (9 hours); training; 30-day support

06.out_scope.v: Accessibility audit and WCAG remediation; content writing, restructuring or rewriting; a true payment gateway (Stripe, Ebix) or WinBEAT NEXT API; client portal; photography and video; SEO retainer; Google Ads; annual third-party subscriptions

06.future.v: Client portal via WinBEAT NEXT API (12 to 18 months); SEO retainer (reopen 6 to 8 weeks pre-launch); Revive Media photography; Google Ads; ongoing content production

06.sensitivities.v: Signature comment: "discussions on new site map will overrule that listed within contract". Quote describes 12 verticals and 13 product lines; the client's new sitemap is about 109 to 125 pages. Directors' top concern is scope creep: anything new is quoted in writing first. Rate locked at $195 for the project

08.photography.v: Very few own images: a couple of older team photos. Wants real operating environments (boats, trucks, mine sites), not stock office shots

08.icons.v: Wants a standalone element pulled from the logo (like Centrewest's C) and a custom icon set reusable across marketing

08.video.v: Hero video preferred (stock, showing the range of operating environments); auto image slider is the fallback. Boat to road to mine site transition idea

09.sitemap_status.v: DRAFT. Mia committed to send it for approval after 21/07; no approval date recorded

09.total_pages.v: About 109 unique pages before Insights articles (count from Website 2.0 Flow v2); handover says about 125
09.total_pages.contested: Quote: 12 industry verticals and 13 policy/product lines [E]. Client's new sitemap: about 109 pages [D], about 125 [H]. Client signed with 'discussions on new site map will overrule that listed within contract' [E]. Handover says proceed on the new sitemap [H]. Pages are fine if served by the quoted templates; extra templates are not.
09.total_pages.why_client: Your new sitemap has grown well past the original structure, so we'd like to agree which page templates carry it before design goes further.

09.top_nav.v: About, Risk, Sector, Insights, Contact as a horizontal mega menu. Middle groupings are labels, not pages

09.utility_nav.v: Request Quote, Lodge Claim, Lodge Workplace Injury

09.footer.v: AFSL 233 765 disclosure and legal entity name are non-negotiable, plus compliance links

11.designs_quoted.v: 5 internal templates named in the quote (Contact, industry landing, policy/product, Our People, blog/news), plus "internal page designs as required"

11.hours.v: Not split in the quote. Internals share the 34 design hours with the homepage

11.deliverable.v: Desktop and mobile per template ("designed for both mobile and desktop")

11.start.v: After logo sign-off and homepage approval

11.order.v: Product/policy template first (it carries about 66 pages), then sector index, Our People, contact and forms, insights, legal

12.features.v: See 06.in_scope. Plus hover effects and micro-interactions, video and image support, spam protection

12.plugins.v: Gravity Forms and Rank Math Premium under PWD agency licences (no cost while hosted with PWD)

12.integrations.v: Quoted: DEFT (Macquarie) outbound link, EDM (Mailchimp, Campaign Monitor or equivalent, which one not known), LinkedIn feed. Client raised Stripe on 21/07 as Macquarie may change
12.integrations.contested: Quote: outbound link to DEFT (Macquarie), no gateway [E,H]. Client on 21/07: Macquarie may change, Stripe 'back on the table' [T 26:24]. Mia said devs would integrate it [T 27:16]. A Stripe integration is not quoted.
12.integrations.why_client: If Macquarie's payment portal is changing, we need to know which payment option you land on, as it changes what we build on the Pay an Invoice page.

12.forms.v: General enquiry with a subject dropdown for inbox filtering; "review my policy" form dropped; claim and workplace injury forms with PDF upload stay. Which inbox each subject goes to is not known

12.accessibility.v: No WCAG target: audit and remediation are out of scope. Build to sensible defaults

12.performance.v: Fast load is one of the client's main aims; avoid graphic-heavy pages

12.seo.v: Keep permalinks and rankings, 301s, GA4 and GTM retained, schema, separate the brand from WTW in search. Access to GA4, GTM and Search Console not confirmed

12.browsers.v: Mobile and tablet friendly across all breakpoints

13.writer.v: Client writes all copy (Isabella's team). PWD places and splits it into sections

13.status.v: About four fifths drafted on 21/07, then to be checked by their team. Current status not known

13.tone.v: Professional, assured not aggressive, expert but relatable, clear and concise, not overly corporate

13.in_time.v: Content was due by development, "about 6 weeks" after 21/07. No firm date was set

13.internal_content.v: Product page copy in progress; roughly half the leaf pages had no coverage list on 21/09

14.intricacies.v: Sitemap rewritten mid-sale (Risk and Sector pillars); some middle menu tiers must not become pages; payment link may switch from DEFT to Stripe; two names for the main contact (Popov and Breheny) in CRM and email

14.risks.v: Page count far above the quoted template list on 34 design hours; Stripe would be new scope; copy and leaf content late; few own photos; three coordinators in four months

14.politics.v: Isabella is the firm's first marketing hire and PWD's internal champion; her standing depends on this landing. Directors fear scope creep

14.legal.v: FSG and Terms of Business, Insurance Brokers Code of Practice, Privacy Policy, Disclaimer, Complaints, Vulnerable Client and Financial Hardship policy, AFSL footer

14.gut.v: Strong, organised client, but momentum has slipped (meeting moved for illness, team away, coordinator change). Rebuild trust with a clear plan on 27/10

feel.aim: Bold, assured, modern, clean, credible. Simple but with some interest (light animation, layered horizontal segments)
feel.avoid: Generic broker, hectic or graphic-heavy (Knightcorp), childlike colour, cold sterile corporate, thin type with no presence

references.take: Simple but aesthetic balance, horizontal bars, light animation, gradient within one hue
Boat to road (to mine site) transition, segments
references.leave: Heavy media if it slows load

references.take: A letter or mark pulled from the logo into page design
references.leave: Anything that makes WT look like a competitor

hard_nos.dislikes: Client names and logos on the site (privacy, client poaching); a colour scheme close to any competitor or WTW; cloudpg mobile stacking
hard_nos.rejected: Pay an Invoice on the homepage; separate review-my-policy form
hard_nos.sector: Real operating environments (marine, mining, road) over stock office imagery
